title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous and next pages. P is an additive category of semi-simplicial ('½ simpliciaux') k-module complexes. Q = P_1 is the full subcategory of 'perfect' objects, those whose L_i, Z_i, B_i, H_i are free of finite type. Σ is a class of distinguished (split-type) short exact sequences, so (P, Σ) is a relative exact category in the sense of Hochschild / Eilenberg–Moore. Two families of objects matter: the 'cells' C^i and the unit object Ψ^0 = 1_*.
- The Σ-injectives form the additive subcategory K generated by the C^i: acyclic, 'flasque' objects.
- The Σ-projectives form the additive subcategory P_0 generated by the C^i together with Ψ^0.

The page opens by finishing a parenthesis from the previous page. K (sums of C^i) does not have enough Σ-projectives; one must add Ψ^0. There are enough Σ-injectives (and Σ-projectives) also in the larger category P. By standard relative homological algebra, any two Σ-injective (or Σ-projective) resolutions are homotopy equivalent, uniquely up to homotopy.

Relative Ext. Ext_Σ^i(L, M) can be computed equally by injective or projective resolutions, or both at once. For i ≥ 1 these agree with the usual hyperext of the underlying complexes L and M. For i = 0 they do not: Ext^0 is Hom in P, which differs from Hom in the derived category.

Derived functors. Let F : Q = P_1 → P → B be a k-additive functor to an abelian category. Its right or left relative derived functors are defined through Σ-injective or Σ-projective resolutions. The key invariant is H^i(F) := R^iF(Ψ^0), cohomology 'with coefficients in F', by analogy with Γ(F) = F(Ψ^0).

Grothendieck then gives a functor-category interpretation:
- Consider k-additive, Σ-left-exact functors P → B. Such a functor is determined by its values on K, the full additive category on the cells C^i.
- An additive functor on K is the same thing as a cochain complex C^· = F(C^·) in B. Hom(C^i, C^j) is essentially generated by the differential C^i → C^{i+1}, with d^2 = 0.
- So this functor category is equivalent to B^·, the category of cochain complexes in B.
- Under this equivalence, Γ : F ↦ F(Ψ^0) becomes C^· ↦ Z^0(C^·) = H^0(C^·), by left exactness applied to Ψ^0 → C^0 → C^1.
- The right derived functors of Z^0 on B^· are the H^i(C^·), i ≥ 1. So H^i(F) are the derived functors of Γ.

Finally, C^· is itself a Σ-injective resolution of Ψ^0, so RF(Ψ^0) ≃ F(C^·) in the derived category; the next page adds '(dim. dans cat. dérivée)'.

Purpose: set up a 'cohomology of the unit with coefficients in an additive functor' on perfect semi-simplicial complexes. This prepares the multiplicative (tensor) structure on P_*, Q, P_0, K introduced on the next page, and the dévissage of ∂-perfect complexes.
errors: 'For i≥1 Ext_Σ^i = usual hyperext' is plausible only under the hypothesis, tacit on the page, that Σ-injectives are acyclic and Σ-exact sequences are degreewise split. For i=0 the relative Hom differs from the derived-category Hom, which Grothendieck acknowledges.
The equivalence 'Σ-left-exact additive functors P→B ≃ B^·' requires that every object be Σ-copresented by objects of K. This was asserted ('assez d'injectifs') but not proved on the page.
Several readings are uncertain (the i=0 case, the parenthesis about restricting the F). No outright mathematical error is visible.

ideas.what: Relative (Σ-)exact structure on semi-simplicial complexes, with Σ-injectives = additive hull of cells C^i and Σ-projectives = cells plus the unit Ψ^0; enough of both; uniqueness of resolutions up to homotopy
ideas.modern_name: Relative homological algebra / exact category with enough projectives and injectives
ideas.where_published: Not as such; the general idea is close to Tôhoku-style axiomatics

ideas.what: Relative Ext agree with hyperext for i≥1 but differ at i=0
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of relative Ext with Ext in the derived category / stable-category Hom

ideas.what: H^i(F) := R^iF(Ψ^0) as derived functors of Γ: F ↦ F(unit) on the category of Σ-left-exact additive functors, identified with cochain complexes in B so that Γ = Z^0 and H^i(F) = H^i(F(C^·))
ideas.modern_name: Functor cohomology / Yoneda-type identification of exact functors on a category of cells with complexes (Dold–Kan / Freyd-style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Freyd, Mitchell; cohomology of small categories (Roos, Quillen)
ideas.where_published: Spirit close to the treatment of Γ and derived functors in Tôhoku and SGA 4

ideas.what: RF(Ψ^0) ≃ F(C^·) because the cellular complex is a Σ-injective resolution of the unit
ideas.modern_name: Computation of derived functors by acyclic (cellular / flasque) resolution

missed.claim: The page sets up a relative-homological framework (cells C^i Σ-injective, unit Ψ^0 needed for projectives) intended to carry a tensor structure and a 'dévissage' of perfect semi-simplicial complexes. The interplay of this exact structure with ⊗ (begun on the next page) is not a standard published object, but this page itself is routine.
missed.quote: la cat. K des sommes de C^i [n'a pas] assez de Σ-projectifs, il faut y rajouter Ψ^0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: it resembles later tensor-exact / Frobenius-type setups in tensor-triangular geometry, but nothing concrete beyond standard material appears here.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard relative homological algebra: enough Σ-injectives and Σ-projectives, Ext comparison, derived functors evaluated on the unit, and the identification with Z^0 / H^i of cochain complexes. It is interesting only as context for the unpublished multiplicative dévissage project.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'n'a pas assez de Σ-projectifs, il faut y rajouter Ψ^0 ...)' rather than 'contient par assez' (the Σ above 'projectifs' is a superscript).
'On [?] a [?] d'objets injectifs' is likely 'On a assez de Σ-injectifs [et projectifs] aussi dans la plus grande catégorie P'.
'L. et de M.' is plausibly 'L_* et de M_*' (hyperext of the two complexes).
'(ex.t. à gauche' is likely 'exacts à gauche', with 'Σ-' written above: the category of k-additive Σ-left-exact functors P → B.
'quelle cette catégorie est équivalente à' is likely 'que cette catégorie est équivalente à B^·'.
'est identifié au' is likely 'est identifié au foncteur C^· ↦ Z^0(C^·) = H^0(C^·) sur B^·'.
In 'F(C·)' at the bottom, the C^· corrects an earlier letter.
